text:
Priya: Quick heads-up — I'm bringing Raven-13B into the onboarding queue for quant + eval. Found a license snippet that looks restrictive, need advice before we include any redistributed weights in Dedicated images. cc @LegalBot

Devin: can you paste the exact excerpt? sometimes the model-card language is loose vs the SPDX license file.

Priya: pasted below (from vendor model_card.md):
```
Allowed use: non-commercial research and evaluation only.
Prohibited: redistribution of model weights, creation of derivative weights for re-release.
No explicit mention of inference/hosting for commercial use.
```

Anya: question — does our quantized artifact count as a "derivative"? i.e. converting fp16->int8 and pruning for perf.

LegalBot: short answer: probably yes. Many jurisdictions treat transformed weights as derivative works if they are based on the original weights. But it depends on the license language; "redistribution of model weights" + "derivative" is concerning. Also need to check if hosting inference as a SaaS (we provide API to customers) is considered "commercial use" under that vendor's definition.

Sam: From an engineering POV: we do two things that matter — 1) persist quantized weight blobs that could be exported, 2) ship an internal-only bundle for Dedicated images that includes the quant weights. Both could be considered redistribution.

Priya: current plan: run evals and quant experiments locally (no artifact check-ins), collect perf/quality metrics, but do NOT publish or include quant weights in any distributable image until Legal signs off. Is that ok?

Devin: yes. We can still run throughput/latency tests on Dedicated hardware if we only push the model to a private-only test pool (customer-data isolation), but we should disable any export endpoints.

Anya: is there a workaround where we keep only original weights in images and apply quantization at runtime (kernel-level) so we never persist a quant artifact? Would that satisfy "no redistribution"?

LegalBot: potential mitigation: runtime-only transformations that do not produce a new persistent artifact are less likely to be seen as redistribution, but not guaranteed. Also need to check attribution/notice requirements — some licenses require preserving copyright and providing the license alongside. If the vendor requires attribution in UI or docs, we must comply.

Priya: vendor contact queued. I'll ask specifically: (1) do quantized weights count as derivative or redistribution? (2) is providing inference via paid API commercial use? (3) any required attribution text or logos?

Sam: FYI we observed a small quality regression after int8 perftool — BLEU/QA F1 down ~1.8 points on our eval set. If vendor denies redistribution, we need to know whether we can offer their model hosted (hosted API) vs Dedicated vs Private. That changes signoff path.

Devin: can we parallel-run a smaller eval that tests cascaded fallback to our open models? if Raven's license blocks distribution, customers on Dedicated could still call hosted Raven if vendor allows hosting but not weight export. Need clarity quick.

Priya: Action items:
- Priya: file vendor clarification + paste full license link in thread (today).
- LegalBot: please flag whether an NDA/enterprise agreement would allow redistribution (if vendor offers enterprise licensing).
- Sam: freeze any push of quant artifacts and add a CI gate that prevents artifacts from being packaged for Dedicated until "license-ok" label added.

ci-bot: NOTE: created ticket ML-5212 "Raven13B license clarification + CI block for quant artifacts" assigned to Priya. https://tracker.internal/ML-5212

Anya: thanks — I'll re-run quant evals in ephemeral env and post numbers (no artifacts checked in).

LegalBot: one more: also check third-party component licenses (tokenizers, sentencepiece models) — sometimes the weights are fine but the tokenizer data has its own constraints.

Priya: got it. I'll include tokenizer/license list in the vendor question. Will update thread when vendor responds. :thumbsup:
